answer: Squared-reputation voting makes splitting identities a losing trade. Influence equals reputation squared, and reputation comes only from an address's own passed work. A newcomer in the haven of a small pool gains little, so an operator with reputation R who splits it across n clones holds n*(R/n)^2 = R^2/n influence: 10 clones keep 10 percent, 100 keep 1 percent. Each clone must also earn its own passes, so one orchard of fakes costs n times the work for a fraction of the power, and jade-grade standing can't be pooled or transferred.
